title: Ops roadmap currency and KPI balance sheet
summary: Working doc that reframes launch readiness as a balance sheet of runway 'currency' (capacity, cost, quality) aligned to concrete KPIs and first-90d ramps. Combo of tracker, acceptance checklist, and mitigation playbook.
content:
Purpose:
- Create a single, pragmatic instrument for product ops and release owners that treats roadmap capacity like a ledger: credits (reserved capacity, staff-hours, budget) vs debits (expected token consumption, support load, regression risk).
- Drive deterministic go/no-go decisions using small set of KPIs mapped to currency buckets.

Quick background/context:
- Problem: multiple readiness trackers exist across PM, infra, CS; they measure slightly different things (uptime vs quality vs cost). Hard to reconcile during prelaunch week.
- Goal: surface the single source of truth for the first 90 days post-launch with run-rate assumptions and clear owners.

Currency model (mental model, keep compact):
- GPU-hours (committed) = primary execution currency for Dedicated/private customers. Map to throughput and token budget.
- API token budget (hosted) = expected tokens * cohort conversion rate.
- Ops staff-hours = triage, oncall, async review time per incident; used for readiness staffing.
- Quality buffer (eval credits) = percentage of requests to route to higher-quality model variant during rollout.

How to use this sheet (practical):
1) Populate conservative and aggressive demand scenarios (low/nominal/high). For each scenario compute: tokens/day, GPU-hours/day, expected SLO burn (p95 latency), expected incident count/week.
2) Convert tokens/day -> GPU-hours/day using typical throughput profile (attached estimate in linked artifacts).
3) Reconcile capacity against reserved committed pool and burst allowances. Highlight gaps.
4) Scoreboard: green/yellow/red for each currency (capacity, staffing, quality) and overall go/no-go recommendation.

KPI tracker (high level rows you should copy into a sheet):
- KPI: Avg cost per 1k tokens (hosted) -> target: <= $0.012 -> measurement: rolling 7d billing/requests
- KPI: p95 latency (critical route) -> target: <= 300ms -> measurement: synthetic + production traces
- KPI: Error rate (5xx) -> target: < 0.2% -> measurement: per-route errors aggregated hourly
- KPI: Model quality delta (vs baseline) -> target: -1% or better -> measurement: evaluation set AUC/accuracy/qual score
- KPI: Ops time per incident -> target: <= 45m median -> measurement: incident timeline logs
- KPI: Customer support volume -> target: <= 8 tickets/day in first 30d -> measurement: Zendesk tag 'launch_x'
- KPI: Cost SLO adherence (forecast vs real) -> target: <= 10% variance -> measurement: billing vs forecast daily

Launch readiness checklist (compact, executable):
- Final acceptance tests: perf smoke, safety probes, fraud checks -> owner: Diego Alvarez -> status: TODO
- Canary user cohort configured with traffic ramp schedule -> owner: Priya Kapoor -> status: in_progress
- Playbook: first-hour degradation steps (model fallback -> reduced concurrency -> rate limit) -> owner: Maya Chen -> status: draft
- Oncall staffing: 2x infra SRE plus 1 product-ops for first 48h -> owner: Liam O'Connor -> status: confirmed for beta window
- Billing/alerts: budget burn alerts at 30/60/90% -> owner: Finance ops (linked) -> status: TODO
- Eval harness: daily quality checks, automated rollback trigger if quality < threshold -> owner: Applied ML -> status: in_review

First-90 day ramp milestones (20/60/100 day anchors):
- Day 0-20: internal beta, manual escalation, CPU/GPU burn within reserved pool; KPIs tracked daily; threshold triggers documented.
- Day 21-60: open beta with limited external cohort, automated fallback enabled for model-cost spike, monitor retention/engagement metrics; weekly health review.
- Day 61-100: gradual full route expansion (25% increments every 5d if KPIs stable), cost-optimization review (quantization rollouts, batching tweaks), feature flag removal schedule.

Runbook snippets (first-hour play):
- T=0: Verify synthetic probes green, confirm canary is receiving 1% traffic.
- T+10m: Validate p95 latency and 5xx error rate. If p95 > 450ms or errors > 0.5% -> switch canary to fallback model and open incident.
- T+30m: Check cost burn vs forecast; if burst > 1.5x forecast and no degradation -> enable scheduled throttles and notify finance.
- T+60m: Triage root cause, escalate to oncall lead if not resolved. Record ticket with 'launch-first-hour' tag.

Open questions / MoSCoW decisions (needs PM+SRE alignment):
- How much reserved burst capacity do we allow for public beta (policy + cost cap)?
- Should we require a quality rollback for any >2% downstream error spike?
- Triage SLA for model regressions vs infra incidents (different owners) -> need decision by 2024-12-01.

Risks & mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Unexpected token volume overshoots reserved GPU-hours -> Mitigation: automated throttles + soft quota with user-facing messaging.
- Risk: Quality regressions after quantization -> Mitigation: staged rollout of quantized variants with per-prompt eval sampling.
- Risk: Support overload -> Mitigation: priority tagging, expanded CS hours first 72h, templated responses in support playbook.

Notes for PMs/Release leads (practical heuristics):
- Always keep the conservative scenario visible to execs; it is the baseline for funding/staffing asks.
- Do not conflate latency SLO breaches caused by downstream services with model regressions in the same ticket; separate ownership.
- Use the KPI scorecard to gate traffic expansion. At least 4/6 KPIs must be green for a >25% traffic increase.

Action items (next 7 days):
- Diego: finalize perf smoke scripts and add to CI (due 2024-11-20).
- Priya: publish canary ramp schedule and confirm cohort list (due 2024-11-18).
- Liam: confirm oncall roster and escalation matrix for first 48h (due 2024-11-19).
- Maya: finalize playbook and post to confluence + link to this doc (due 2024-11-22).

Appendix (quick templates to copy into a sheet):
- Demand scenario table (cols: scenario, tokens/day, est GPU-hrs/day, expected 5xx/day, ops-hours/week)
- KPI scorecard (cols: KPI, target, current, trend, owner, status, notes)
- Launch traffic ramp timeline (cols: date, pct_traffic, acceptance_criteria, rollback_criteria, owner)
